summary: This small app creates a Thermostat object set to 72 degrees and prints the status it reports, so you can check the class's behavior with your own eyes.

lines.text: The `new` keyword builds an actual Thermostat object from the class, handing the constructor the starting temperature; write 72.0 rather than 72 because the constructor expects a double.
The plus sign joins the label to the String that getStatus() hands back, so the method is called first and its result becomes part of the printed line.
We chose 72 deliberately: it sits above the heating threshold of 68 and below the cooling threshold of 75, so we already know the answer should be idle before we run the program.

This app class exists only to exercise Thermostat by hand. It works for one scenario, but confirming sixty scenarios this way is exactly the repetitive, easy-to-skip checking that unit tests will replace.
